# News Details


[View All News](https://investors.bitgo.com/news/default.aspx)


### BitGo Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results


November 9, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s21.q4cdn.com/773293151/files/doc_news/BitGo-Announces-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-2026.pdf)


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


BitGo Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: BTGO) (“BitGo” or “the Company”), the digital asset infrastructure company, today reported its financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Q3 2026 Highlights**


- **Normalized Assets on Platform, and Normalized Assets Staked** increased 32% and 41% year-over-year, respectively, reflecting continued growth in institutional adoption.
- **Completed the acquisition of NYDIG’s institutional trading business,** expanding BitGo’s capabilities in derivatives, structured products, and financing and broadening institutional client relationships.
- **Expanded institutional trading and settlement connectivity,** extending the OKX off-exchange settlement integration internationally and introducing BitGo Prime’s Global Liquidity Layer.
- **Net income** of $44.1 million driven by the appreciation of BitGo’s digital asset treasury since Q2’26.
- **Repurchased $24.7 million of common stock** during the quarter under the Company’s $50 million share repurchase authorization.

**Management Commentary**


**Mike Belshe, CEO of BitGo**


“During the third quarter, we continued to strengthen BitGo’s position as a leading institutional digital asset infrastructure platform. We expanded our global footprint and completed the acquisition of NYDIG’s institutional trading business. We also expanded our off-exchange settlement network through partnerships and integrations with leading exchanges and liquidity providers.


Security and asset protection have been central to BitGo since our founding, and we believe our regulated security infrastructure represents an important competitive advantage as institutional adoption accelerates. BitGo’s Go Network offers a differentiated model that allows institutions to maintain their assets in a regulated, national bank while accessing an expanding network of trading venues, products, and liquidity. This gives institutions greater trading flexibility and choice while reducing their exposure to exchange counterparty risk. We believe this combination of security, asset protection, and market access represents an important evolution in institutional digital asset infrastructure.


At the same time, we are positioning BitGo to provide the financial infrastructure for bringing traditional assets on-chain, beginning with tokenized equities. We see significant opportunities to broaden access to U.S. equities through existing digital asset and stablecoin networks, while expanding the utility of traditional investment portfolios through on-chain settlement, collateral, and financing applications. We believe this convergence of traditional finance and blockchain infrastructure significantly expands our addressable market and creates new opportunities to leverage BitGo’s regulated financial services platform, institutional relationships, and expanding financial capabilities.”


**Consolidated Financial Highlights**


- **Assets on Platform:** Reported Assets on Platform declined to $59.9 billion from $65.2 billion in the prior quarter, primarily due to lower median digital asset prices used in calculating the metric. On a normalized basis, adjusting for differences in median prices between periods, Assets on Platform and Assets Staked increased slightly sequentially. Based on September 30, 2026 digital asset prices, quarter-end Assets on Platform were $83.0 billion and Assets Staked were $16.3 billion.
- **Total Revenue** was $2.9 billion, down 34.1% sequentially and 50.9% year-over-year, driven primarily by lower digital asset sales activity as a result of a continued soft crypto trading environment. Direct costs 5 decreased 34.3% sequentially and 51.1% year-over-year, respectively. Total revenue after direct costs were $37.3 million, representing a decline of 12.1% sequentially and 32.1% year-over-year.
- **Operating Expenses** (excluding direct costs) were $56.6 million, decreased 5.5% sequentially as a result of cost reduction initiatives initiated in the second quarter.
- **Net Income** was $44.1 million compared to net loss of $19.0 million in Q2 2026 and net income of $22.7 million in Q3 2025. The sequential and year-over-year improvement was primarily driven by a $71.5 million unrealized gain on the Company’s digital assets treasury during the quarter.
- **Adjusted EBITDA** **Loss** was $4.3 million compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $4.2 million in Q2 2026 and an Adjusted EBITDA profit of $13.5 million in Q3 2025. The sequential decline was primarily driven by lower revenues and margins during the quarter, partially offset by lower operating expenses.
- **Diluted EPS** was $0.36 compared with diluted EPS of ($0.16) in Q2 2026 and $0.15 in Q3 2025.
- **Balance Sheet:** $143.2 million of cash and cash equivalents and no corporate-level debt other than borrowings used to fund our lending activities. In addition, our corporate treasury held 2,399 company-owned Bitcoin with a fair value of $200.4 million as of September 30, 2026.

- **Digital Asset Sales:** Revenue was $2.7 billion, down 35.2% sequentially and 52.0% year-over-year. After digital asset sales costs, contribution margin was $4.2 million, representing 15 basis points, compared to 17 basis points in Q2 2026 and 20 basis points in Q3 2025. Performance was impacted by softer trading activity and a higher mix of lower-margin stablecoin transactions.
- **Staking:** Revenue was $68.2 million, up 5.4% sequentially but down 24.1% year-over-year. Staking fees totaled $64.2 million, representing a take rate of 5.9% compared to 6.0% in Q2 2026 and 9.7% in Q3 2025. Normalized Assets Staked increased 0.5% sequentially and 41.1% year over year to $10.5 billion. The sequential revenue growth was driven by higher ETH balances and prices, partially offset by lower protocol reward rates and price declines across other tokens. The year-over-year revenue decline primarily reflected a lower take rate driven by changes in client mix.
- **Subscriptions and Services:** Revenue was $25.6 million, down 7.2% sequentially and 24.5% year-over-year. The sequential decline primarily reflected lower non-recurring engineering (NRE) revenue due to project timing.
- **Stablecoin-as-a-Service:** Revenue was $37.4 million, down 3.8% sequentially and up 52.5% year-over-year. Stablecoin sponsor fees were $34.5 million, resulting in a take rate of 7.7%, compared to 8.0% in Q2 2026 and 3.6% in Q3 2025. The sequential decline primarily reflected lower average reserve balances, while year-over-year growth was supported by higher reserve balances and fixed monthly fees from newly supported stablecoin programs.


**Conference Call and Webcast Information**


BitGo will host a call to discuss its results at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time today, November 9, 2026. A live webcast of the conference call will be available online at[https://investors.bitgo.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.bitgo.com&esheet=54637775&newsitemid=20261108455835&lan=en-US&anchor=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.bitgo.com&index=1&md5=c46058c8465a1bf3795b82d39a3e9bef) , and an archived replay will be accessible at the same location for up to one year.


**About BitGo**


BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit[www.bitgo.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.bitgo.com&esheet=54637775&newsitemid=20261108455835&lan=en-US&anchor=www.bitgo.com&index=2&md5=1e9c3807ec51b6978ad67f98aae7b4a1) .

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


We have provided in this release financial information that has not been prepared in accordance with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP financial measures are not based on any standardized methodology prescribed by GAAP and are not necessarily comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. We use these non-GAAP financial measures internally in analyzing our financial results and believe they are useful to investors, as a supplement to GAAP measures, in evaluating our ongoing operational performance. We believe that the use of these non-GAAP financial measures provides an additional tool for investors to use in evaluating ongoing operating results and trends and in comparing our financial results with peer companies, many of which present similar non-GAAP financial measures to investors.


Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures provided in the Appendix below.


*Adjusted EBITDA* : We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss), excluding (i) provision for income taxes, (ii) depreciation and amortization, (iii) stock-based compensation expense, (iv) employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions, (v) net changes in unrealized appreciation (loss) on digital assets, (vi) certain non-recurring charges (which are specified in detail below), and (vii) restructuring charges. The above items are excluded from our Adjusted EBITDA measure because they are non-cash in nature, their amount and timing are volatile and influenced by digital asset prices, they are unpredictable, or they are not driven by the core results of operations. In any case, including such items would reduce the comparability of our financial performance across periods and with industry peers. We believe that Adjusted EBITDA provides useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our results of operations, as well as providing a useful measure for period-to-period comparisons of our business performance in a consistent manner. Moreover, Adjusted EBITDA is a key measure used by our management internally for financial, risk management and operational decision-making.
